title: Breakfast News: A $5.7 Billion Flex or Genius?
author: Tmf Breakfast News
description: Salesforce acquires Braze for $5.7 billion to strengthen its marketing capabilities, with Braze stock jumping 50%. Netflix faces growth challenges with slowing revenue and weak ad performance. SpaceX beats expectations with 161% revenue growth, while Intuitive Surgical falls despite beating estimates due to cooling U.S. procedure growth. Tesla, Meta, and IBM report earnings with major capital spending decisions in focus. EQT continues steady cash flow growth as a natural gas producer.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Acquisition of Braze is strategically sound and relatively inexpensive, but long-term growth prospects are limited to 7-10% annually rather than historical 20%, suggesting modest upside potential.
Stock surged 51% on acquisition announcement; company has strong financials with $300M+ net cash, improving margins, and 25%+ annual topline growth at reasonable valuation.
Stock fell 6% after hours due to slowing revenue growth (12%, slowest in 3 years), weak ad revenue below targets, and minimal viewing hour growth (2%), indicating fundamental growth challenges.
Stock fell 7% despite beating earnings estimates because U.S. da Vinci procedure growth slowed to 10%, lagging overseas growth and signaling weakening domestic demand momentum.

Facing investor scrutiny over $130-145B capex guidance for 2026; needs strong Q4 revenue outlook (~$73.6B) to convince market that spending is justified, with historical precedent of capex spikes dragging stock down.
Recovering from prior quarter delays in software and mainframe deals; Q3 software revenue should confirm momentum, but upcoming guidance will be key driver of stock direction.

title: Why Dell Technologies Stock Took a Dive Last Week
author: Howard Smith
description: Dell Technologies stock plummeted 22.9% following a Barclays downgrade that questioned the pace of enterprise AI adoption. Analysts argued that recent server revenue growth stems primarily from memory component cost inflation rather than fundamental AI demand, with hardware representing only about a quarter of corporate AI budgets. The sell-off reflects investor concerns about whether massive AI infrastructure investments will materialize into sustained corporate purchases.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock declined 22.9% following Barclays downgrade from buy to hold. Analysts raised concerns that server revenue growth reflects cost inflation pass-through rather than genuine AI adoption acceleration, threatening the company's growth narrative and near-term revenue trajectory.
Issued a downgrade on Dell, citing concerns about the sustainability of enterprise AI spending and questioning whether hardware demand reflects real adoption or temporary cost factors.

title: Quantum Computing Is Still Years Away. These 6 Stocks Show Who Is Closest to Real Revenue.
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: Quantum computing companies remain years away from profitability, with most relying on stock sales rather than customer revenue. IBM has the financial capacity to wait until 2028-2029, IonQ shows real revenue growth but heavy cash burn and dilution, while D-Wave and Rigetti have promising bookings but minimal revenue. Alphabet and Nvidia are positioned as bystanders rather than quantum revenue stories.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong balance sheet with $10 billion committed to quantum over five years, funded by profitable mainframe and software operations. CEO expects profitability by 2028-2029. Has scale with 13 utility-scale systems and $1 billion in cumulative quantum business.

Only pure-play with meaningful revenue ($144.7M in H1 2026, up from $28.3M), showing real commercial traction. However, operating cash burn nearly tripled to $254.8M over six months, and share dilution increased 47% year-over-year, offsetting revenue growth benefits.

Bookings surged 1,120% to $35.5M in H1 2026 with 67.7% commercial revenue, showing promise. However, actual revenue remains tiny at $3M quarterly, and company is funding operations through at-the-market stock offerings rather than customer sales.

Revenue grew from $1.8M to $5.1M quarterly, and holds $541M cash with no debt. However, still burning cash and relying on repeated at-the-market stock offerings to fund operations, indicating customer revenue insufficient to cover expenses.

title: Can Slightly Higher Consulting Revenues Aid IBM's Q3 Earnings?
author: Na
description: IBM is projected to report Q3 2026 Consulting revenues of $5.348 billion, up slightly from $5.324 billion year-over-year. Growth is expected to be driven by AI partnerships with Sarvam and Arm, digital transformation services, and the Logiq Consulting acquisition strengthening cybersecurity capabilities. However, the company's Earnings ESP of -0.63% suggests no earnings beat is predicted.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While IBM shows marginal revenue growth in Consulting (+0.45% YoY) and strategic initiatives through AI partnerships and acquisitions, the negative Earnings ESP of -0.63% with a Zacks Rank #3 suggests the market does not expect an earnings beat, limiting upside potential.

title: Can Healthy Increase in Software Revenues Benefit IBM's Q3 Earnings?
author: Na
description: IBM is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 21 with Software segment revenues projected to reach $7.62 billion, up from $7.21 billion year-over-year. The company's $240 million partnership with Together AI to expand cloud infrastructure for enterprise AI inference, along with collaborations on cybersecurity and AI-powered innovations, are expected to drive growth. However, the Zacks model does not predict an earnings beat for the quarter.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While IBM shows positive revenue growth expectations (+5.7% for Software segment) and strategic AI/cybersecurity partnerships that support long-term prospects, the Zacks model predicts no earnings beat for Q3 2026 with a negative ESP of -0.63% and Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting limited upside surprise potential in the near term.

NVIDIA benefits from IBM's $240 million Together AI deal involving deployment of NVIDIA's HGX B300 systems and Spectrum-X Ethernet networking on IBM Cloud, demonstrating continued enterprise demand for NVIDIA's AI infrastructure and computing technologies.
